{{Quote|Within the last several months, there have been two distinct occurrences that suggest the presence of an espionage Droid ''[sic]'' within the New Republic's Ministry of Supply.|General Airen Cracken, ''Wanted by Cracken''|<ref name="WBC" />}}
'''T5-G3''' was a [[Supervisor droid/Legends|labor management droid]] who worked in the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic's]] [[Ministry of Science (New Republic)|Ministry of Science]], modified by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] to operate as an [[espionage droid]]. Around [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], the droid was twice detected by the New Republic sending short transmissions from its supply convoys. While the short nature of the transmissions allowed T5-G3 to avoid detection, a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] of eight thousand [[Credit chip/Legends|credits]] was issued for the droid's capture. This information was noted in [[General/Legends|General]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken's]] [[Datafile/Legends|datafile]] of persons of interest to the New Republic, ''[[Wanted by Cracken]]''.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Both times, the transmissions were so short that the communications specialists aboard the convoy ships couldn't get a fix on the source of the signal, allowing the Droid ''[sic]'' to escape undetected.|General Airen Cracken, ''Wanted by Cracken''|<ref name="WBC" />}}
[[File:AirenCracken-WBCp4.png|thumb|left|250px|Airen Cracken, who included T5-G3's activities and bounty in his datafile]]
T5-G3 was a [[Supervisor droid/Legends|labor management droid]] working for the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic's]] [[Ministry of Science (New Republic)|Ministry of Science]] in a role that allowed it to coordinate the tasks of other [[Droid/Legends|droids]]. The droid was modified by [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] to [[Spy/Legends|spy]] on the New Republic and provide information and data to the rival government. These modifications&mdash;including subversive [[Programmer/Legends|programming]] and a concealed [[subspace tight-beam transmission core]] with which to communicate with the Empire&mdash;resulted in a short in T5-G3's [[Logic display sensor|logic dispenser]]. This short adjusted the personality and behavior of T5-G3, who would occasionally act in a quirky manner.<ref name="WBC" />

On two separate occasions<ref name="WBC" /> around [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]],<ref name="time">[[Wanted by Cracken (sourcebook)|''Wanted by Cracken'']], which establishes T5-G3's activities in the previous [[Standard month/Legends|months]], is set three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], which the ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. ''Wanted by Cracken'' must therefore be set in [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]] and T5-G3's activities around this [[Time/Legends|time]].</ref> T5-G3, by then an [[espionage droid]], was detected by the New Republic sending tight beam transmissions from [[Starship/Legends|vessels]] in the government's supply convoys. These transmissions were short, which allowed T5-G3 to avoid and escape detection as the convoy's [[Communications officer/Legends|communications specialists]] could not identify the source of the transmissions. In preparation for additional transmissions, [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]] installed special sensor packages onto ships within the convoys that would allow them to pinpoint T5-G3's location [[Standard second|seconds]] after a transmission was detected.<ref name="WBC" />

In 7 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]],<ref name="time" /> New Republic [[General/Legends|General]] and [[Director of New Republic Intelligence|Supreme Commander of Intelligence]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]] released a [[Datafile/Legends|datafile]] of persons of interest to the New Republic. Titled ''[[Wanted by Cracken]]'', it included the limited known information of T5-G3&mdash;the detected transmissions made by an unknown droid&mdash;and a general caution to the New Republic's agents regarding espionage droids in a section titled "Special Cases." T5-G3's detected activities resulted in a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] of eight thousand [[Credit chip/Legends|credits]] to be issued for its capture. As T5-G3's exact droid model was not known, an image of a standard [[3PO-series protocol droid/Legends|3PO-series protocol droid]] accompanied the entry within ''Wanted by Cracken'' to demonstrate the generic and innocuous nature of espionage droids.<ref name="WBC" />

{{RPGseed}}
A group of New Republic agents were tasked with finding and capturing T5-G3 after the release of ''Wanted by Cracken''. They successfully located the espionage droid due to a combination of the droid's increasingly unusual behavior and the installed sensor packages in the convoys.<ref name="WBC" />
{{Endgame}}

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|It seems likely that the Droid has dual-mode programming: the surface programming is that of whatever role the Droid is supposed to be serving. Beneath that is the secondary espionage programming, which compels the Droid to broadcast as much information as possible to whoever has sent the Droid.'' [sic]''<nowiki />|General Airen Cracken, ''Wanted by Cracken''|<ref name="WBC" />}}
[[File:3POespionagedroid.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The image of a 3PO-series protocol droid used in the entry for T5-G3 in ''Wanted by Cracken''.]]
T5-G3 had a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] body with a single head, two [[Limb/Legends|arms]], and two legs. The modifications to T5-G3 meant the droid had dual-mode programming&mdash;the droid would complete its normal functions as a labor management droid, unaware of actions completed as part of the espionage droid's programming. The droid's role allowed it to order other droids to retrieve data or perform a set of tasks, passing the correlated data to its programmers. T5-G3 could even [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipe]] and reprogram those droids that questioned these orders. While average labor management droids could be described as quirky, the changes to T5-G3 meant the droid was especially quirky. These behavioral eccentricities would increase in severity: the droid's performance would be hindered after six to eight [[Standard month/Legends|months]], before the droid would cease functioning completely.<ref name="WBC" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|Often, the only way to detect an espionage Droid is to physically disassemble the Droid and try to find the programming boards for the espionage functions&mdash;a time consuming process indeed.'' [sic]''<nowiki />|General Airen Cracken, ''Wanted by Cracken''|<ref name="WBC" />}}
T5-G3 had a [[AA-1 VerboBrain/Legends|AA-1 VerboBrain]], a [[Broadband antenna/Legends|broadband antenna receiver]], a [[TranLang III communications module/Legends|TranLang III communication module]] loaded with over seven million [[Language/Legends|languages]], and a [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]]. It also had two [[Audio sensor/Legends|audio sensors]] and two [[Photoreceptor/Legends|visual sensors]], all attuned to the [[Human/Legends|Human]] range of vision and hearing.<ref name="WBC" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|It's just a 3PO clone.... I'll be it ''[sic]'' an EVIL one! Sorta like 3PO-Bender|Rob Caswell|<ref name="RobDA">{{DeviantArt|username=robcaswell|url=robcaswell/art/Spy-Droid-350104750|name=[[Rob Caswell]]|text=Spy Droid}}</ref>}}
T5-G3 was mentioned in the [[West End Games]]' [[1993]] sourcebook [[Wanted by Cracken (sourcebook)|''Wanted by Cracken'']], written by [[Louis J. Prosperi]] for the company's ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''. The book uses a separate page with notes identifying T5-G3 for the [[Wikipedia:Gamemaster|gamemaster]], keeping the identity and nature of the espionage droid secret to player characters. Illustrator [[Rob Caswell]] provided an image of a 3PO-series [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] to depict T5-G3.<ref name="WBC" />

Caswell felt that the image of the droid was iconic but boring given it required no original design in its creation. Despite this, Caswell felt the image was "clean" and was impressed by the technical aspect of the image to a degree that they were surprised this was one of their own artworks. Caswell also likened the droid to the character [[Wikipedia:Bender (Futurama)|Bender]],<ref name="RobDA" /> a foul-mouthed robot from the animated television series [[Wikipedia:Futurama|Futurama]].<ref name="Bender">{{WebCite|url=https://screenrant.com/futurama-season-8-bender-john-dimaggio-hulu-cast-response|text=Futurama Bender Voice Actor Speaks Out On Not Returning For Reboot|author=Graham-Lowery, Nathan|date=2022-02-10|work=[[Wikipedia:Screen Rant|Screen Rant]]|archivedate=20220405173408}}</ref>
